newsitem.title: FRANCE: France aims for 1997 GDP/deficit of 3.3 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: France aims for 1997 GDP/deficit of 3.3 pct - paper.

text.p: France is aiming to reduce its public deficit as a percentage of gross domestic product to 3.3 percent in 1997 and three percent in 1998, French daily Liberation said on Friday, citing an unnamed senior official.

The newspaper quoted the official as saying that although there was no official target in the spending guidelines sent recently to ministers by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, the route being followed was towards 3.3 percent this year.
The newspaper quoted the official as saying the deficit could be brought down to "3.3 percent of GDP this year" from 4.2 percent last year.
"Germany is in a difficult situation and has elections in the autumn of 1998. It will not be able to be very strict next year," the paper also quoted the official as saying.

Liberation said the government was looking to find 30 billion francs to bring the 1997 deficit down from around 3.7 percent, which it said was the level forecast by finance ministry's budget division, to 3.3 percent but "without austerity".
The paper also quoted a government adviser as saying there was some concern that Germany would pull out the stops to hit three percent in 1997 and that this could cause problems.

"If they post a deficit similar to ours in 1997, 3.2 or 3.3 percent, everything's alright. But if they decide to reinforce their austerity programme to reach three percent come what may, there will be a real problem," the adviser was quoted as saying.
It said the adviser declined to say what the French government's response would be in this situation.
"We are not in that scenario," the adviser said.
